study: NCB - native planner check on the manuscript's headline benchmark corpus (exp1b)
review_item: 17_p3-wardrop-mapf-guidance_REVIEWS.md P1 - 'Rerun incumbent-preserving search with a proper validation/test split and a native planner check'; R2 'Test the tie rule on a native planner'
question: Do the guidance fields this paper builds keep their ordering, and does its tie-binning remedy keep its effect, when the planner is third-party compiled code instead of this repository's Python PIBT?

native_arm.planner: Kei18/lacam3 commit 55347c8, PIBT::set_new_config, compiled unmodified from the vendored clone at ../mapf-throughput-envelope/_probes/ext/lacam3
native_arm.task_generation: native: its own C++ std::mt19937 seeded by --seed; uniform distinct starts over the largest connected component; uniform i.i.d. goals over that component, or alternating pickup/station legs on the warehouse map
native_arm.guidance_injection: table[i][u] = floor(dist_w(u -> goal_i) / eps_tie), dist_w = weighted shortest path in the directed guidance-weighted graph (Dijkstra on the reverse graph). With eps_tie = 1 this is exactly lacam3's own integer distance semantics plus its own uniform [0,1) tie-breaker, so the native arm tests the guidance field and the tie rule together.
what_is_independent: planner logic and its swap detector
what_is_NOT_independent: the guidance weights themselves are this repository's fields, exported arc by arc - that is what is under test
the map geometry is this repository's, exported to octile .map and re-parsed by lacam3's own parser
the lifelong protocol (uniform goal law, warehouse alternation, elapsed-time priorities, throughput definition) is this paper's specification, reimplemented in C++
the native planner has NO equivalent of this repository's tau=20 stall escape, and its swap detector is upstream's, not ours

matrix.comparator: results/summary_v2.json ['headline'], the frozen Python arm of exp1b (same maps, fleet sizes, methods, 10 seeds, 1000 steps)

endpoints.throughput: completed goals per timestep over the measured window (warmup 0), identical to the Python arm's definition
endpoints.mean_task_delay: sum of completed-task durations divided by the number of completions
endpoints.wait_fraction: agent-steps spent standing still divided by agent-steps

comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.per_cell: for each of the 15 (map, N) cells, d_TU = mean(tolls) - mean(unweighted) and d_TL = mean(tolls) - mean(lanes), computed the same way in both arms
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.C1_sign_tolls_vs_unweighted: PASS iff sign(d_TU) agrees between arms in at least 11 of 15 cells
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.C2_sign_tolls_vs_lanes: PASS iff sign(d_TL) agrees between arms in at least 11 of 15 cells
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.C3_level: PASS iff the median of |T_native - T_python| / T_python over the 45 (map, N, method) groups is at most 0.10
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.C4_headline_open_map: PASS iff on room-32-32-4 at N=170 and at N=270 the native arm has d_TU > 0 and d_TL > 0 (the paper's strongest claim)
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.C5_tie_rule: PASS iff the native tolls arm at eps_tie = 0.01 has strictly lower mean throughput than at eps_tie = 1.0 in at least 11 of 15 cells
comparison_rule_declared_in_advance.on_failure: a failed criterion is reported as a disagreement between the reimplementation and native code, in the paper and in the response ledger; no cell is dropped, no criterion is retuned, and no native-equivalence claim is made beyond what passes

provenance_checks.export_round_trip: the exported arc weights must re-read bit-identically to common.build_weights output
provenance_checks.vertex_set: the driver's reported |V| and |largest component| must equal this repository's free-cell count for the map
provenance_checks.python_arm_reproduction: one stored exp1b Python condition is re-run from the current code and must reproduce its frozen throughput exactly

retention: every attempted cell is written to results/native_check/runs_bench/ regardless of outcome
supersedes_note: The first registered native check (native_check_protocol.json, SHA fccb50907bdeb0f36a4eedfd1743942e4e2bafbdd3d4aa7554b83403251061a2) was scored against results/table_headline.csv, which belongs to the SUPERSEDED procedural exp1 corpus, not to the exp1b benchmark corpus the manuscript headlines. That check and its 480 cells are retained unchanged in results/native_check/runs and results/native_check/summary.json; this protocol repeats it against the corpus the manuscript actually reports. Neither run is discarded.
